summary: Duty to protect CPNI; customer approval for use/disclosure; authentication before call-detail disclosure, account-change notices, training/discipline, annual officer compliance certification (64.2009(e)); breach notification (64.2011).
applies_to: Telecommunications carriers and interconnected VoIP providers (TRS providers under parallel rules).
size_thresholds: No size exemption in current rules. Delayed 2023 amendment would exempt from FCC/law-enforcement notice breaches affecting fewer than 500 customers where no harm is reasonably likely.
status: Current 64.2011 in force (LE notice within 7 business days). 2023 Data Breach Reporting Order (FCC 23-111, 89 FR 9968) expanded 'breach' to covered PII and added FCC notice; Sixth Circuit DENIED petitions for review on Aug 13, 2025 (Ohio Telecom Ass'n v. FCC), but the 64.2011 amendments remain 'delayed indefinitely' pending an FCC effective-date notice (eCFR current through 2026-09-23 still shows old text).

summary: Report qualifying communications outages: notification within 120 minutes (wireline example), initial report within 72 hours, final report within 30 days.
applies_to: Wireline, wireless, cable, satellite, interconnected VoIP, covered 911 providers, submarine cable licensees.
size_thresholds: Thresholds are outage-based (duration >= 30 minutes and user-minute / 911 / special-facility criteria), not company size.

summary: Carriers must ensure lawful-intercept capabilities are activated only with lawful authorization; appoint senior officer, maintain SSI policies and records, file SSI plans with FCC.
applies_to: Telecommunications carriers (incl. facilities-based broadband and interconnected VoIP).
status: In force. FCC's Jan 2025 declaratory ruling reading CALEA sec. 105 to impose broader cybersecurity duties was rescinded by Order on Reconsideration adopted Nov 20, 2025 (90 FR 58006).

short_name: FCC submarine cable landing license national-security rules
summary: Licensing and national-security conditions/certifications for submarine cable and SLTE owners/operators, including reporting requirements.
applies_to: Submarine cable landing licensees and SLTE owners/operators.
status: First order effective Nov 26, 2025 (some sections delayed); Second Report and Order effective Sept 25, 2026 except listed sections delayed indefinitely.

citation: 6 U.S.C. 681b; proposed 6 CFR Part 226 (89 FR 23644, Apr 4, 2024)
summary: Will require covered critical infrastructure entities to report covered cyber incidents to CISA within 72 hours and ransom payments within 24 hours.
applies_to: Covered entities in critical infrastructure sectors as defined in the final rule (scope still being refined).
size_thresholds: Proposed rule included size-based criteria tied to SBA small-business standards plus sector-based criteria; final scope TBD.
status: NOT YET IN EFFECT: no final rule published as of 2026-09-25. CISA held additional town halls (Feb and May 2026 notices) to refine scope and burden before a final rule. Statutory reporting duties apply only once the final rule is effective.

citation: 17 CFR 229.106 (Reg S-K Item 106); Form 8-K Item 1.05 (Release 33-11216, 88 FR 51896)
summary: Annual 10-K disclosure of cyber risk management, strategy and governance; Form 8-K Item 1.05 disclosure of material cybersecurity incidents.
applies_to: Exchange Act reporting companies (public issuers), including public companies in any sector.
size_thresholds: No exemption by size; smaller reporting companies received a later Item 1.05 compliance date (June 15, 2024 vs. Dec 18, 2023).
status: In force; effective Sept 5, 2023. No rescission found in Federal Register as of 2026-09-25.
